title.narrative: Ecuador - Sustainable Family Farming Modernization Project

description.narrative: The development objective of the Sustainable Family Farming Modernization Project for Ecuador is to enhance incomes of small and medium sized farm households by supporting more productive and climate-smart use for land and water. The project comprises of three components. The first component, investments for climate-smart sub-projects consists of following two sub-components: (i) productive investments; and (ii) improvement of agricultural, water, and soil management practices. The second component, capacity building for institutional stakeholders and beneficiaries organizations will focus on improving and supporting the outcomes of the subproject investments of component one. The third component, project management will support: (i) the functioning of the central unit of the project implementation unit (PIU) to be installed within the under-secretariat of irrigation and drainage in the ministry of agriculture, livestock, aquaculture, and fisheries (MAGAP) in Quito and; (ii) eligible costs and staffing related to the project on seven decentralized offices of MAGAP (Zonales).
The project development objective is to enhance incomes of small and medium sized farm households by supporting more productive andclimate-smart use of land and water.

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator (achieved: 80.2%) was calculated based on information supplied by the PIU.</p>

title.narrative: Number of training days provided to MAGs or GADs staff

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was defined as the increase in the land used for agricultural production within a given year in the area benefiting from subproject irrigation investments. Its measurement accounts for multiple cropping of a given piece of land within the same year. The indicator was calculated for three different groups of subprojects: (i) for subprojects in group 1, the end value was 21.60 (overachieved: 144.00 percent); (ii) for subprojects in group 2, the end value was 9.19 (overachieved: 183.80 percent); (iii) for subprojects in group 3, the end value was 2.63 (achieved 52.60 percent of end target). However, the monitoring surveys (database and 3 waves of surveys) were fully completed only for group 1, and therefore the result achieved by this group was used for demonstrating the indicator achievement.</p>

<p>The first indicator (achieved: 95.9%) measured the number of training days received by project beneficiaries, calculated as the number of users of the irrigation infrastructure who concluded the training sessions delivered, multiplied by the number o days of each session.</p>
<p>The second indicator (overachieved: 198.7%) measured the number of training days received by female project beneficiaries, calculated as the number of female users of the irrigation infrastructure who concluded the training sessions delivered, multiplied by the number of days of each session.</p>

title.narrative: Clients who have adopted an improved agr. technology promoted by the project

comment.narrative:
<p>This indicator (overachieved: 179%)<strong> </strong>reflected the total number of subproject investment users who have adopted an improved agricultural technology promoted by the Project, considering that: (i) the agricultural technology is new for the producer; (ii) was directly promoted by the Project; (iii) there is evidence of its use in situ. Examples of such technologies include improved soil management; improved crop or livestock management; improved application and handling of crop protection agents and/or fertilizers, and agrochemicals, and/or use of different types; improved post harvest practices etc.</p>
<p>The second indicator (overachieved: 362%) reflected the number of female subproject investment users who have adopted an improved agricultural technology promoted by the Project.</p>

title.narrative: Operational water user associations created and/or strengthened (number)

comment.narrative:
<p>The first indicator (overachieved 108%) reflected the number of subprojects that received capacity strengthening from the Project (through the Capacity Building and Technical Assistance Programs - PCATs).</p>
<p>The second indicator (achieved 99%) reflected the number of subprojects with specific arrangements (established following the subproject’s recommendations) related to maintenance and operation.</p>

title.narrative: Operational water user associations created and/or strengthened (number)
Water users provided with new/improved irrigation and drainage services (number)

comment.narrative:
<p>The first indicator (achieved 100%) represents the total number of users from the subproject investments in irrigation and drainage. A total of 6,014 water users - each user representing a household - benefited from the subproject investments. Overall, an estimated 25,000 people – consisting of all the household members – benefited from subproject investments.</p>
<p>The second indicator (achieved 100%) reflects the total number of females benefiting from the subproject investments in irrigation and drainage.</p>

title.narrative: Area provided with irrigation and drainage services (ha)

comment.narrative:
<p>The first indicator (achieved 100%) measured the total agricultural area benefiting from the subproject investments in irrigation and drainage, including new area (extension of area irrigated) and rehabilitated area (improvement of existing irrigation and drainage systems).</p>

<p>The second indicator (achieved 100%) measured the total agricultural area benefiting from the subproject investments in new irrigation and drainage.</p>

<p>The third indicator (achieved 100%) measured the total agricultural area bnefiting from the subproject investments in rehabilitated irrigation and drainage.</p>

title.narrative: Sub-projects with post-project community engagement or O&M arrangements (%)

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator (achieved 99%) reflected the percentage of the total number of subprojects implemented where there exist specific community agreements (established following the subproject’s recommendations) related to maintenance and operation of the irrigation system.</p>

title.narrative: Average annual net income per ha on area benefited by the project

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator (92% achieved) was monitored in three groups of beneficiaries of the subprojects showing different results: (i) in group 1, the value achieved was US$409.69; (ii) in group 2, the value achieved was US$506.10; and, (iii) in group 3, the value achieved was US$342.65. However, complete surveys waves (4 waves) were collected only for the first group of beneficiaries (consisting of 11 subprojects, whose full subproject cycle completed in 2020). In consequence, the achieved value compared with the end target reflects the results measured for subprojects in group 1 only. The indicator value reflects the net income by hectare, defined as the sum of all net revenues divided by the total area monitored. The methodology included the following: (i) through a participatory process, a representative group of families whose production systems are under the subproject is identified - these families/groups are then registered in the monitoring system; (ii) information regarding each product in the production systems benefiting from the subproject investments is gathered, including: annual production volume, revenues from production sold, production costs, annual average price (which is kept as a constant for future calculations); (iii) annual net income is calculated; (iv) the value obtained is converted into values per hectare/year; (v) all net per hectare incomes obtained are added and divided by the respective total cultivated area (under each subproject).</p>
